prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1399; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened for a side impact collision at a signalized intersection. Insured vehicle was struck on the driver side by a third-party vehicle that entered on a red signal, per initial statements. Police report requested. Claimant reported a wrist injury at the scene and was transported for evaluation.

Entry 2: Claimant has retained counsel. All further contact to be routed through the attorney's office. Letter of representation received and filed. Requested itemized medical records and treatment history through counsel. Reserve set pending evaluation of the injury.

Entry 3: Imaging results reviewed. Claimant diagnosed with a fracture of the wrist, treated with immobilization and referred to an orthopedic specialist. Attorney advised that a follow-up consultation is scheduled and that surgical options are still being evaluated. Will reassess reserve once treatment plan is confirmed.

Entry 4: Liability review in progress. Third-party driver's insurer has acknowledged the claim but has not accepted fault. Traffic camera footage from the intersection requested and is pending. Based on the statements gathered so far, liability appears clear against the third party, though comparative fault is still being assessed.

Entry 5: Received demand package from claimant's counsel including medical bills, wage loss documentation, and a narrative of ongoing treatment. Demand is under review with the medical bill audit team. Next step is to schedule a file review with supervisor and request an independent medical examination through counsel before any settlement discussions begin.
